knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: The nucleon number is found by basic addition of the stated proton and neutron counts before writing the controlled nuclide notation; no major reusable syllabus physics formula is applied.

hints: The nucleon number is the total number of protons and neutrons.
Put the nucleon number above and the proton number below the element symbol.
walkthrough: The nucleus has 29 protons and 37 neutrons, so its nucleon number is A = 29 + 37 = 66.
Its proton number is Z = 29 and its element symbol is Cu.

ai_rubric.observable: Gives copper with nucleon number 66 and proton number 29, as ⁶⁶₂₉Cu or an equivalent unambiguous notation.

hints: A single nuclear decay has a fixed energy release.
Use the spectrum to compare that fixed release with the range of beta-particle kinetic energies.
walkthrough: For this decay, the total energy released is fixed.
Fig. 7.1 shows that the beta particles have a continuous range of energies rather than one fixed energy.
The beta particles therefore do not receive all of the fixed decay energy in every event.
Another particle must carry the remaining energy; in beta-minus decay this is an electron antineutrino.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the energy released in a decay is fixed or constant.
Identifies from the spectrum that beta particles have a continuous range of energies rather than a constant energy.
Concludes that another particle, specifically an antineutrino if named, carries the remaining energy.

hints: The stated decay is beta-minus decay.
Recall the neutral lepton emitted with the electron in beta-minus decay.
walkthrough: A β⁻ particle is an electron emitted in beta-minus decay.
Beta-minus decay also emits an electron antineutrino.
Therefore the other particle is an electron antineutrino.

hints: In beta-minus decay, the nucleon number is unchanged and the daughter proton number increases by one.
Include both the beta-minus electron and the electron antineutrino, each with nucleon number zero.
walkthrough: The parent is ⁶⁶₂₉Cu. In beta-minus decay its nucleon number remains 66 and its proton number rises to 30, giving ⁶⁶₃₀Zn.
The emitted beta-minus particle is an electron, written ⁰₋₁β⁻ (or ⁰₋₁e).
An electron antineutrino is also emitted, written ⁰₀ν̄ₑ.
The completed equation is ⁶⁶₂₉Cu → ⁶⁶₃₀Zn + ⁰₋₁β⁻ + ⁰₀ν̄ₑ.

ai_rubric.observable: Gives parent ⁶⁶₂₉Cu and daughter ⁶⁶₃₀Zn with their nucleon and proton numbers correct.
Includes a beta-minus electron as ⁰₋₁β⁻, ⁰₋₁e, or equivalent notation.
Includes an electron antineutrino as ⁰₀ν̄ₑ or equivalent notation.
